data.why: The repository ships with no data (dashboard/static/data only has a .empty_data placeholder); the real pipeline needs BAM files, minimap2 and Nextclade, so instead these TSV/JSON files are written directly in the exact schema the Django loader (dashboard/services/data.py and dashboard/services/pileup.py) expects, covering ~8 weeks, 13 virus types across 9 Swiss cantons, a PCR/sequencing mismatch, a missing Match flag, an unmappable location code, two co-infected samples, and genome-coverage data for SARS-CoV-2 and RSV (including a failed/near-zero sample and a planted RSV-A G-gene coverage gap vs. an unaffected RSV-B sample).

goals: check this week's sequencing and PCR detection counts on the home page to see which respiratory viruses are currently circulating
open a virus's page and read the weekly time series and canton map to see where and when it has been detected
inspect the genome coverage (pileup) plot for a virus to spot samples or genome regions with poor sequencing depth
compare PCR and sequencing detections for a given week to see how often the two methods agree
open the co-infection page to see which virus pairs occur together in the same sample and in what fraction of detections
drill into one co-infected sample to see the sequencing depth of each virus it carries

review.summary: The tree captures the dashboard's purpose well: an overview of circulation, per-pathogen time and place by assay, genome-coverage quality and co-infection patterns. Its eleven sampled screens are faithful, with only the PNG-download task lacking its own evidence. It should be fixed before filing: phylogenetic placement and the per-sample co-infection depth drill-down, two of the README's headline uses, appear only as notes, and a generic chart-export task sits in the wrong phase.
